definition: A sentence structure where the subject performs the action, making writing clearer and more direct.
exampleSentence: Use active voice to make every instruction clear and direct for the reader.

definition: A callout block — note, warning, tip — that draws attention to important supplementary information.
exampleSentence: Add a warning admonition before the step that deletes user data.

definition: Linking to a specific section within a document using a URL fragment identifier.
exampleSentence: Anchoring the link to a specific section saves the reader from scrolling.

definition: Documentation describing every endpoint, parameter, and response of an API exhaustively.
exampleSentence: The API reference lists every parameter, its type, and an example value.

definition: Tailoring technical content to the specific knowledge level and goals of its intended readers.
exampleSentence: Strong audience awareness means you don't explain git to senior engineers.

definition: A visually distinct block highlighting critical information separate from the main body text.
exampleSentence: Put the security warning in a callout so it stands out from the rest of the text.

definition: A single versioned record describing what changed, was fixed, or was added in a release.
exampleSentence: Every changelog entry should say what changed and why the user should care.

definition: Inline text within source code explaining why something is done, not just what it does.
exampleSentence: A good code comment explains the why, not the what — the code already shows the what.

definition: Triple backticks in Markdown that wrap a code block and optionally declare its language.
exampleSentence: Always use a code fence with a language tag so the syntax gets highlighted.

definition: Informal or conversational language that may be unclear or culturally specific to some readers.
exampleSentence: Avoid colloquialisms in docs that will be translated or read by non-native speakers.

definition: Expressing information using the fewest words necessary without losing meaning or accuracy.
exampleSentence: Conciseness means cutting every word that doesn't add information for the reader.

definition: A defined category of documentation — tutorial, how-to, reference, explanation — each with a distinct purpose.
exampleSentence: Decide the content type before writing — is this a tutorial or a how-to guide?

definition: A link or pointer directing readers to related content in another section or document.
exampleSentence: Add a cross-reference to the authentication guide at the start of this section.

definition: A documented warning that a feature or API will be removed in a future version.
exampleSentence: Add a deprecation notice to warn users before removing the old endpoint.

definition: A documentation framework organizing content into tutorials, how-tos, references, and explanations.
exampleSentence: We restructured the docs using the Diátaxis framework to separate tutorials from references.

definition: Clarifying which of multiple possible meanings or uses of a term is intended in a given context.
exampleSentence: A disambiguation note clarifies which definition of model applies in this context.

definition: A structured comment inside a function or class that describes its purpose, parameters, and return value.
exampleSentence: A docstring at the top of the function explains the parameters and return type.

definition: Treating documentation like source code — versioned in Git, reviewed via PRs, and built automatically.
exampleSentence: Docs-as-code means every change to the docs goes through a pull request review.

definition: Explicit documentation of unusual or boundary scenarios a system handles or intentionally excludes.
exampleSentence: Good edge case documentation tells users what the system does with empty inputs.

definition: Documentation written to remain accurate over time without frequent updates tied to a specific version.
exampleSentence: Write evergreen content that stays accurate without needing constant updates.

definition: A piece of documentation focused on building conceptual understanding rather than guiding a task.
exampleSentence: An explainer helps readers understand why JWT authentication works the way it does.

definition: Metadata at the top of a Markdown file — title, date, tags — parsed by static site generators.
exampleSentence: The front matter at the top of the file sets the page title and description.

definition: An alphabetical list of domain-specific terms with their definitions within a documentation site.
exampleSentence: Link unfamiliar terms to the glossary so readers can look them up immediately.

definition: A goal-oriented document walking a competent user through steps to complete a specific task.
exampleSentence: A how-to guide walks you through setting up authentication in your app.

definition: A writing style using command verbs — click, open, run — standard in step-by-step instructions.
exampleSentence: Use the imperative mood in steps: click, open, run, not you should click.

definition: The cues — links, headings, labels — that help readers predict whether following a path will pay off.
exampleSentence: Strong information scent means users can predict what's behind every link.

definition: Monospace-formatted text within a sentence used to reference code values, filenames, or commands.
exampleSentence: Format the variable name with inline code so it stands out from the surrounding text.

definition: A JavaScript documentation standard using tagged comments to describe functions and types.
exampleSentence: JSDoc comments on exported functions are picked up automatically by the IDE.

definition: A searchable collection of articles and guides helping users solve problems independently.
exampleSentence: The knowledge base gets fifty percent of its traffic from search engines.

definition: Adapting content for a specific locale — language, date formats, cultural references — beyond translation.
exampleSentence: Good localization adapts date formats and units, not just the language.

definition: The opening sentence that summarizes the most critical information, front-loading the key point.
exampleSentence: Put the key information in the lede so skimmers get the point immediately.

definition: A lightweight markup language using plain-text syntax to produce formatted HTML documents.
exampleSentence: All our documentation is written in Markdown and stored alongside the code.

definition: An extension of Markdown that allows embedding React components directly inside documentation files.
exampleSentence: MDX lets us embed a live code playground directly inside the documentation page.

definition: Short UI text — labels, error messages, tooltips, placeholders — that guides users through an interface.
exampleSentence: Good microcopy on the error message tells users exactly how to fix the problem.

definition: The visible text of a link or menu item that sets reader expectations about the destination.
exampleSentence: A clear navigational label sets the right expectation before the user clicks.

definition: A string of multiple nouns used as modifiers that creates ambiguous, hard-to-parse phrases.
exampleSentence: User account management interface settings page is a classic noun pile — rewrite it.

definition: Guides designed to help new users or developers reach their first success as quickly as possible.
exampleSentence: Strong onboarding documentation gets new users to their first success in minutes.

definition: A specification format for describing REST APIs in a machine-readable YAML or JSON file.
exampleSentence: The OpenAPI spec is the single source of truth for all our API endpoints.

definition: A sentence structure where the subject receives the action — often vaguer and harder to follow.
exampleSentence: The form was submitted is passive voice — submitted the form is clearer.

definition: Writing that communicates clearly to its intended audience without unnecessary complexity.
exampleSentence: Plain language guidelines say to avoid words with shorter, clearer alternatives.

definition: A condition or setup step that must be completed before following a guide or tutorial.
exampleSentence: List every prerequisite at the top so users don't get stuck halfway through.

definition: Structuring documentation to reveal complexity gradually as the reader advances.
exampleSentence: Progressive disclosure hides advanced options until the user is ready for them.

definition: Ordinary written language as opposed to structured formats like bullet lists or tables.
exampleSentence: A short paragraph of prose before the steps gives useful context without slowing readers down.

definition: The entry-point document of a repository describing its purpose, setup, and usage.
exampleSentence: The README is the first thing a new contributor reads, so keep it focused.

definition: User-facing documentation summarizing what changed, improved, or was fixed in a product release.
exampleSentence: Release notes should highlight what changed for users, not for engineers.

definition: A step-by-step operational guide for handling a specific incident or routine system procedure.
exampleSentence: Follow the runbook step by step when you get paged for this kind of incident.

definition: The ease with which a reader can skim a document and extract the most relevant information.
exampleSentence: Scannability improves when you use short paragraphs, headings, and bold key terms.

definition: Writing content once and reusing it across multiple documents or output formats.
exampleSentence: Single sourcing means you update the authentication guide once and it updates everywhere.

definition: A short, self-contained code example illustrating a specific concept or API usage.
exampleSentence: A good code snippet is short enough to copy and run without modification.

definition: A written document detailing the requirements, behavior, and constraints of a feature or system.
exampleSentence: Write the spec before the code so everyone agrees on what is being built.

definition: A document defining writing conventions — voice, tone, terminology — for consistent communication.
exampleSentence: The style guide says to use second person and present tense throughout the docs.

definition: A navigational list of headings linking to sections within a long document.
exampleSentence: A table of contents at the top helps readers jump straight to what they need.

definition: The degree to which documentation correctly reflects the actual behavior of a system.
exampleSentence: Technical accuracy means every code sample in the docs has been tested to work.

definition: The specific set of terms defined and used consistently across a product and its documentation.
exampleSentence: Consistent terminology across the docs prevents confusion about the same concept.

definition: Abbreviation for table of contents — often auto-generated from document headings in doc tools.
exampleSentence: The TOC is auto-generated from headings so it stays up to date automatically.

definition: The personality and attitude expressed through writing — formal, friendly, direct, empathetic.
exampleSentence: The tone of voice in error messages should be helpful, never condescending.

definition: A learning-oriented document guiding a beginner through a complete working example step by step.
exampleSentence: A tutorial guides a beginner from zero to a working example by the end.

definition: The practice of crafting all interface text — labels, errors, onboarding — to guide user behavior.
exampleSentence: Good UX writing on the empty state tells users exactly what to do next.

definition: Maintaining separate documentation sets for each major release of a product or API.
exampleSentence: Versioned documentation lets users of older releases find the right information.

definition: The consistent personality and character expressed across all written content for a product or brand.
exampleSentence: The product's voice is warm and direct, never robotic or overly formal.

definition: A guided explanation of a process or codebase, often used in reviews or onboarding sessions.
exampleSentence: The onboarding walkthrough shows new users the three most important features.

definition: A vague qualifier — easily, simply, just — that implies something is straightforward when it may not be.
exampleSentence: Remove the word simply — it's a weasel word that makes users feel bad when they struggle.

definition: The deliberate discipline of achieving maximum clarity with the minimum number of words.
exampleSentence: Word economy means every sentence earns its place on the page.
